doc.title: Terri Lyne Carrington interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003

title: The Adderleys, family friends
summary: Nat Adderley had her play in Boston at fourteen; she describes the Adderleys as warm, family-like people and notes how Miles, Wayne Shorter and Herbie differ on stage.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: Right. You said about horn players it makes me think of Louis Hayes said something about he watched Cannonball and Nat’s rear ends for years.
But he would get time from that.

That is pretty funny. Yeah. Those guys were really close friends with my dad. So they came to my house a lot when I was young. Cannonball died when I was kind of young but Nat came over several times and he actually had me play with him in Boston when Jimmy Cobb couldn’t. He played a week and I think Jimmy Cobb couldn’t make a couple of the nights and so I played a few nights, and I was fourteen. That was a lot of fun.
What struck you about him, anything in particular? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -7-

He was a down home cat. He was just almost like part of the family you know. They were just beautiful people. And the people that they surrounded themselves with were all beautiful people. It seemed like they had a real grasp on the fact that life is what is important and life inspires music. To me, depending on how you live and how you view life and your philosophies, you know, obviously that affects your musicality and your artistry and so people that like to have a good time in life and are warm, compassionate and engaging kinds of people, that’s how their music is. And you can hear that in Adderleys’ music.
They both were into engaging their audience through the music and also speaking.
Not everybody is good at it.

Yeah this is true. There is, I mean everybody’s different. I mean I don’t have a problem with the Miles Davis — not approach — but just how he was. I might have a problem with somebody that’s trying to be like Miles. But I mean Miles was naturally Miles. Wayne Shorter is naturally Wayne Shorter. He doesn’t talk a lot on stage. Herbie Hancock talks a lot on stage. I think that you just accept people for what they’re offering you and you obviously have the choice to embrace it or not.
